title: Hazel and the Parish
premise: August Coldharbour, a night-shift dispatcher who quietly solves missing-person cases no one else will touch, takes on the file of Hazel Voss, a parish organist vanished for three years and presumed dead. But Hazel's diary, delivered anonymously to his desk, keeps writing entries dated after her disappearance—entries that describe August's own dispatch office in unsettling detail. Following the diary's clues through the parish's respectable facades, August uncovers a witness-protection scheme gone wrong: Hazel faked her death to escape testifying against a beloved deacon, but someone has been keeping her captive ever since. In the end, August finds Hazel alive on the eve of the deacon's fraud trial, exposes the parish network that hid her, and must choose between handing her to the law or helping her disappear again—choosing, at last, to be seen himself.
about_author: Marguerite Okonkwo is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people the justice system overlooks, from a farmhouse office full of case files she probably shouldn't own.
